title: Who batted better in the four matches?
description: Two batters' runs in four matches are compared on the board by the highest score, by the total, and by the difference between the highest and the lowest. Keeko doubts that the batter with the single highest score must be the better one.
teaching_notes: One idea: one measure can hide the rest, so compare several, such as the highest score, the total and the difference between highest and lowest. Watch for students who pick the batter with the single biggest score.

source: Shubman scored 0, 17, 21 and 90 in four matches. Yashasvi sc
video_script.why: The child can read two rows of runs but has not seen that the highest score alone does not decide who batted better.
video_script.substitution: A batter's series is judged by the highest score, the total and the difference between highest and lowest together.
video_script.anchor: A table of runs in four matches for two batters
video_script.wrong_answer: is better, because ninety is the highest score of all
video_script.wrong_move: judges the whole series by one big score

final_answer.value: {{NAME_3}} batted better: total 175 against 128, and a smaller difference, 49 against 90
final_answer.spoken: the second batter did better, with a total of one hundred and seventy five against one hundred and twenty eight, and a smaller difference of forty nine against ninety

names.{{NAME_2}}: batter whose four scores are compared
names.{{NAME_3}}: the other batter in the same four matches

maths_rules: 175 - 128 = 47 runs more in the same four matches
49 is less than 90, so the second batter is more consistent
video_script.design: A two-row table of runs. Three measures are written under it one at a time, and the board ends with the three results side by side.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a table from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>It shows the runs scored in a cricket series of four matches.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>{{NAME_2}} and {{NAME_3}} are the two batters.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Who do you think performed better?

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>We can compare the two batters in three ways.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>One is the highest score, and one is the total.
One is the highest score take away the lowest score.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>A small difference means the scores stay close together, and that is called being consistent.

beats.on_screen: Given: {{NAME_2}} scored 0, 17, 21, 90; {{NAME_3}} scored 67, 55, 18, 35, in four matches

marks.given: the two rows of runs are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, {{NAME_2}} scored zero, seventeen, twenty one and ninety in four matches.
{{NAME_3}} scored sixty seven, fifty five, eighteen and thirty five.

marks.find: the words performed better are underlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find who performed better.

marks.s1: the largest number in each row is circled
marks.s2: the two circled numbers sit side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, find the highest score of each batter.
<bookmark mark='s2'/>{{NAME_2}} has ninety, and {{NAME_3}} has sixty seven.

marks.d1: the rule add the runs is written
marks.d1b: the first row is added to its total
marks.d2: the second row is added to its total
marks.d3: the gap between the totals is marked

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Step two, add the runs of each batter to get the total.
<bookmark mark='d1b'/>{{NAME_2}} has zero plus seventeen plus twenty one plus ninety, which is one hundred and twenty eight.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>{{NAME_3}} has sixty seven plus fifty five plus eighteen plus thirty five.
That makes one hundred and seventy five.
<bookmark mark='d3'/>Both played four matches, so the totals compare fairly, and the gap is forty seven runs.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, highest minus lowest: 90 − 0 = 90; 67 − 18 = 49; 49 is less than 90

marks.c1: the highest and the lowest of each row are marked
marks.c2: the two gaps are drawn as bars of different length

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>Step three, take away the lowest score from the highest.
{{NAME_2}} has ninety take away zero, which is ninety.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>{{NAME_3}} has sixty seven take away eighteen, which is forty nine.
The smaller difference of forty nine shows the more consistent batter.

beats.on_screen: Answer: {{NAME_3}} batted better: total 175 against 128, and a smaller difference, 49 against 90
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>{{NAME_3}} batted better in this series.
The total is one hundred and seventy five against one hundred and twenty eight.
The difference is forty nine against ninety.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's thought bubble shows the 90 enlarged with a crown; the other three scores 0, 17 and 21 light up beside it and the crown is struck through

marks.doubt: the bubble with the crowned 90 appears
marks.fix: the scores 0, 17 and 21 light up beside the 90

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks {{NAME_2}} is better, because ninety is the highest score of all.
Ninety is a fine innings, but it is only one match.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>In the other three matches, {{NAME_2}} made zero, seventeen and twenty one.
<bookmark mark='idea'/>One big score can hide many small ones.
